_readme: Every entry is one node in the tree. To add a food: copy an entry, give it a unique id, set parent to an existing id, and fill in the fields. Ranks in order: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species, variety. A node may skip ranks. Associations (combo meals) live in the separate "associations" list: foods served together but eaten in separate bites. Each lists its member ids; members keep their own place in the tree.

nodes.short: Everything that can be eaten or drunk. Gas station sushi is included under protest.

nodes.trait: Made to be applied to other food, never the star
nodes.short: Sauces, dressings, spreads and blends: things that were made, by extracting, refining, fermenting or combining, so the original would not recognize them. Grown things are never condiments, however they are used. Checked first, because ketchup will try to claim it is a meal.

nodes.trait: Refined until one substance is left
nodes.short: The original would not recognize the result. Sugar from cane, MSG from fermented sugar beets or corn.

nodes.trait: Salts of glutamate, the savory one
nodes.short: Umami, purified.
Form is decided here, not at phylum: texture is a sliding scale.
Supporting cast with an unfair reputation.
Monosodium glutamate and its seasoning kin.
Fermented, then purified to crystals: the last transforming step decides, so it sits with the crystals. Chemically the same glutamate found in tomatoes. Supporting cast with an unfair reputation.

nodes.trait: Several foods ground, pounded or chopped together
nodes.short: Mustard, relish, pesto, salsa, guacamole and spice blends. One food ground alone is still a single food (peanut butter); grind it together with others and it was made.
Mustard, mostly.
Form is decided here, not at phylum: texture is a sliding scale.
Ground seed, vinegar, salt and opinions.
Named on Plate I before it had a card: Fig. 4, Sinapis (praeparata).
Mild, bright yellow from turmeric, and the official mustard of Plate I. Made, so a condiment.
Sharper, made with brown seeds and wine or verjuice. Divionensis: of Dijon.

nodes.trait: Pickled vegetables chopped with sugar and spice
nodes.short: Relish and its relatives.
Form is decided here, not at phylum: texture is a sliding scale.
A pickle that has been through something.
Chopped, sweetened, spooned.
Definitely made, and therefore a condiment. The pickle is a single food; chop it with sugar and spice and the cucumber can no longer pick it out of a lineup. Rules are rules. Fig. 3 on Plate I.
Soy sauce, fish sauce, vinegar, miso and aged hot sauces. The condiment cousins of beer and wine.
Soy sauce and miso.
Form is decided here, not at phylum: texture is a sliding scale.
Pressed and strained after fermenting; straining is finishing, not transforming.
Borrowed from the real soybean genus, as is customary when the soybean is involved.
Fermented, then pressed and strained. Supporting cast for sushi and sashimi. Never the star, however much is poured.
Less salt, same ferment. More or less of the same thing is a variety.
Made with little or no wheat. Its own name, the same ferment: a variety.

nodes.trait: Oil and water forced to agree
nodes.short: Mayonnaise, Caesar, ranch, aioli and vinaigrette.
Mayonnaise and the dressings built on it.
Form is decided here, not at phylum: texture is a sliding scale.
Named for Mahón, which the sauce's most popular origin story credits.
Mayonnaise and aioli.
Oil and egg yolk, emulsified. A condiment, and also an ingredient: deviled eggs call for it, and nothing in the rules forbids a condiment from joining an assembled food.
Form is decided here, not at phylum: texture is a sliding scale.

nodes.trait: Built around anchovy, garlic, parmesan and yolk
nodes.short: Pourable, barely.
Renamed from the generic Condimentum.
Anchovy, garlic, parmesan and egg, emulsified. Supporting cast in the chicken Caesar salad. Cardiniana honours Caesar Cardini, usually credited with the salad.
Ketchup, BBQ sauce, jelly and chutney.

nodes.trait: Tomatoes, cooked down with sugar and vinegar
nodes.short: Ketchup and its relatives.
Form is decided here, not at phylum: texture is a sliding scale.
Spelled either way.
Tomato, reduced.
Tomatoes cooked down with sugar and vinegar: made, so a condiment. Banned from Chicago-style specimens by local statute.
Ketchup with curry spices, as served on currywurst. An add-in, so a variety.

nodes.trait: Fruit juice or pulp cooked down with sugar
nodes.short: Jelly, and other fruit that lost its identity.
Form is decided here, not at phylum: texture is a sliding scale.

nodes.trait: Built around strained fruit juice, set
nodes.short: Jam that lost its identity.
Clear, set, and unrecognizable to the fruit.
Juice extracted, strained and set with pectin. The grape would not pick it out of a lineup, so it was made: a condiment. Jam keeps its fruit and stays a single food.

nodes.trait: Has a beverage role: hydrate, refresh, stimulate or intoxicate
nodes.short: Drinks, sorted by how they were made: ready-made by nature, pressed, steeped, dissolved, fermented, or mixed from other drinks. A milkshake is a dessert wearing a straw, and lives in Constructa.

nodes.trait: Comes out of nature ready to drink
nodes.short: Nothing was squeezed, steeped, dissolved or fermented. Filtering and pasteurizing do not count.
Water, with or without bubbles.
Flat by design.
Water.
The control group.
The baseline every other drink is measured against. Tap or bottled is a vessel question, and the vessel does not count.
Bubbles. The only thing separating these from their still relatives.
Water that fizzes.
Seltzer, club soda, mineral water with bubbles.
Water with bubbles. One order away from tap water, and it will not let you forget it.
From an animal, as nature intended. Plant milks are elsewhere, and they know why.
Flat by design.
Species sorted by animal.
Fat percentage makes a variety, not a species.
The default milk. Whole, 2% and skim are varieties: you still order it as milk.
Nothing removed.
Most of the fat removed. Most of the joy, some argue.
A different animal, so a different species of milk.
Rarely drunk, frequently turned into cheese.

nodes.trait: Squeezed, pressed or strained from a plant
nodes.short: Juices and plant milks: the liquid was already inside the plant, or close to it.
Mostly squeezed fruit by volume. Lemonade fails this test.
Flat by design.
Oranges, grapefruit and relatives.
The breakfast table genus.
Squeezed oranges. Pulp is a variety question the Board refuses to take up.
Pressed orchard fruit.
Pressed apples.
Pressed apples. Once fermented it becomes cider and leaves for Fermentata.

nodes.trait: Strained from grains, nuts or beans, and sold as milk
nodes.short: Pressed and strained from a plant, so not milk. Oat milk is, technically, oat juice. Same idea as Pseudosandwichae, different material.
Flat by design.

nodes.trait: A plant soaked, blended and strained
nodes.short: The family that drew the strongest letters.
Oat, almond, soy and whatever comes next.
Not milk. Oats soaked, blended and strained: oat juice with excellent marketing.
Not milk. Almonds, water and confidence.
Not milk. Soybeans soaked, ground and strained.

nodes.trait: Steeped in hot water or milk, then the solids removed
nodes.short: Coffee, tea and chai: the flavor was pulled out of something that is then thrown away.
Coffee.
Flat by design.
The family most responsible for this website existing past midnight.
Hot water drips or soaks through ground beans, helped only by gravity and patience.
Add-ins make varieties, not new species: you still order it as coffee. A latte is ordered by a different name, so it is a separate species.
Coffee as intended.
Cream and sugar, by New York definition. Listing a variety is not an endorsement of it.
Coffee made under pressure, named for the tan foam on top. Its own line on every café menu.
Hot water forced through finely packed grounds under pressure, in about 25 seconds. Ordered by its own name, so its own species.
nodes.long: Not Expressa. In Expressa the food itself gets squeezed (an orange, an oat). Here the beans sit still and the water is pushed through them, which is steeping in a hurry. Order and family stand: no bubbles (crema is foam, not carbonation), and it is still built around the coffee bean.

nodes.short: Two shots. More of the same thing is a variety.
A short pull: less water, same beans. Has its own name, still the same drink.
A long pull: more water through the same puck. Not an Americano, which adds water afterward.
Tea.
Flat by design.
Black, green and everything between.
Tea from the tea plant. Herbal teas would need a family of their own.
Leaves steeped in hot water. Additions make varieties: you still order it as tea.
Strong black tea with a splash of milk. Steeping time is a matter of national security.
Iced tea sweetened past the point of debate. Southern variety; served by the gallon.
Tea leaves and spices simmered in milk and water, then strained. Still steeped, so still Infusa, and ordered by its own name, so its own species.
nodes.long: A café chai latte, made from a concentrate topped with steamed milk, is two finished drinks mixed together. It would belong with the latte in Miscellae. Not yet collected.

nodes.trait: Things dissolved into water or milk
nodes.short: Sugar, flavor, salts, syrup or cocoa dissolved into water or milk. Where the dissolving happens, in a factory, a fountain or a saucepan, does not matter.

nodes.trait: Sugar and flavor dissolved in water
nodes.short: Soda and lemonade.
Bubbles. The only thing separating these from their still relatives.
Caramel-colored, kola-flavored, endlessly argued over.
The brown sodas.
Can, bottle or 2-liter: same species. The vessel does not count.
Sweetened without sugar. Still ordered as a cola.
Cola with cherry. A variety, not a new species.
Syrup and carbonated water combined at the moment of pouring. Same species as the can; recognized as a variety in honor of everyone who insists the fast-food version tastes better.
The clear sodas.
Clear and citrusy.
Clear citrus soda.
Flat by design.
Mostly water by volume, which is why it is not juice.
The front-yard stand genus.
Not juice. Mostly water with sugar and some lemon juice dissolved in, so it sits with soda, not orange juice.

nodes.trait: Salts and sugar dissolved for exercise
nodes.short: Water with electrolytes. The color is not a flavor.
Flat by design.
Engineered for sweat replacement.
Sold by color.
Salts and sugar dissolved in water. Its purpose is hydration, but the Board sorts drinks by how they are made, not why.

nodes.trait: Cocoa and sugar dissolved into hot milk or water
nodes.short: Chocolate, drunk. Nothing is steeped and thrown away, so it is not Infusa: the cocoa stays in the cup.
Flat by design. A whipped topping is foam, not carbonation.
The family of everything that starts as a cacao bean and ends as a mug.
Named for the cacao tree, Theobroma: "food of the gods." The gods have not commented on its classification.
Cocoa and sugar dissolved into hot milk or water. A drink: it is sipped to warm up, not eaten as a course.
nodes.long: Whether made from a packet, a tin of cocoa or melted chocolate, it is still ordered as hot chocolate, so those are preparations, not species. Marshmallows are an add-in and make a variety.

nodes.short: Yeast or bacteria turned sugar into something more interesting.
Beer. Sometimes called liquid bread; the Board notes that liquid bread is still not a sandwich.
Bubbles. The only thing separating these from their still relatives.
Most beer.
Fermented grain, drunk to unwind.
A drink, not a food: its beverage role wins even though it is assembled from grain, hops, yeast and water.
Sold by the 30-rack. Pale, cold and faintly reminiscent of the stadium it was advertised in.
Brewed in a former auto-body shop and served in a stemmed glass. Named after a local landmark or the brewer's dog. Tasting notes available on request, and also without request.
Wine and cider.
Flat by design.
Wine as most people mean it.
Red, white and the arguments between.
Fermented with the grape skins on.
Fermented with the skins removed.
Bubbles. The only thing separating these from their still relatives.
One order away from still wine.
Wine that fizzes.
Wine with bubbles. Champagne is a regional variety, as the French will remind you.
Two finished drinks combined in real proportion into a new one with its own name: lattes, americanos, cocktails, an Arnold Palmer. A splash into a drink that keeps its name is an add-in instead.
Lattes and their relatives.
Flat by design.
Mostly milk, ordered as coffee.
Lattes, cappuccinos, flat whites.
Not coffee. Espresso and steamed milk, two finished drinks mixed into one with its own name. Mostly milk by volume.

nodes.trait: A finished drink mixed with water, still or sparkling
nodes.short: Drinks of drinks where the second drink is water. Not to be confused with a drink that was only ever watered back to itself: see the restoration rule.
Flat water, flat out.
Built around the espresso shot, lengthened after the fact.
Espresso, made long on purpose. Not a lungo: a lungo pushes more water through the grounds, an americano adds water to the finished shot.
Espresso, then hot water: two finished drinks mixed into a new one and ordered by its own name. A drink of drinks, in the same family tree as the latte, with the good sense to skip the milk.
nodes.long: Legend holds that American soldiers in wartime Italy found espresso too strong and watered it down to taste like home, and that the name was a jab. The record is murkier: the Oxford English Dictionary traces café americano to mid-1950s Central American Spanish and defines it, without ceremony, as "a derisive term for mild coffee." Either way, it was an insult. The Board notes that Americans have a long tradition of taking an insult and printing it on a T-shirt. "Yankee Doodle" began as a British song mocking the colonists, and the colonists adopted it as their own. The americano is the same move in a cup. Told our coffee was weak, we named it after ourselves and ordered a large. The species name, diluta, means "watered down." It is worn with pride. For the record: neener neener.

sources.title: Caffè americano
sources.note: Wikipedia. The wartime story as popular belief; the OED's mid-1950s Central American Spanish origin and its definition, "a derisive term for mild coffee."

nodes.short: Water first, then espresso on top, which keeps the crema. From Australia and New Zealand, hence antipodum. The order of pouring is a preparation detail, so it is a variety, not a species.
Espresso, cold water, ice. Ice is water that has been to the freezer, so nothing new was added.
Where the water arrives carbonated.
The americano's sparkling cousin.
Bitter on bitter, with bubbles.
A shot of espresso poured over tonic water and ice. Two finished drinks, one sparkling, mixed under a new name. Species inquirenda: known from reports, not yet collected by the Board.

nodes.common: One food, bossed around but recognizable
nodes.trait: One whole food, or one nature made, still recognizable to the original
nodes.short: A single food, cut, dried, cooked, ground, smashed, pickled or preserved, that the original would still pick out of a police lineup. Salt and honey count: nature made them. Smashing the whole food passes; extracting a part (juice, oil, refined sugar) fails. The genus is the real genus of the living source.
Fruits, seeds, leaves and roots.

nodes.trait: The fruit of the plant, botanically speaking
nodes.short: Includes the cucumber, botanically a fruit, and the lemon, emotionally a fruit.
The order says what was done to it. Whatever it was, the original still knows it.
Lemons, limes, oranges.
The real genus of the lemon.
A lemon is a lemon, before and after you squeeze it over fish and chips. The table rule: nothing the eater does at the table changes a classification. Its Latin name is the real one.
The order says what was done to it. Whatever it was, the original still knows it.

nodes.trait: The real family of the grape
nodes.short: Grapes, and grapes with life experience.
The real genus of the grape.
A grape with life experience.

nodes.trait: Pickled in brine, or cooked in sugar to keep
nodes.short: The order says what was done to it. Whatever it was, the original still knows it.

nodes.trait: The real family of the cucumber
nodes.short: Cucumbers, squash, melons.
The real genus of the cucumber.
Passes the police lineup test: a cucumber would recognize it instantly. Chop it with sugar and spice, though, and it becomes relish, a condiment.

nodes.trait: The real family of the strawberry
nodes.short: Strawberries, apples, almonds and roses.
The real genus of the strawberry.

Strawberries cooked with sugar to keep them. The fruit is still in there, and the strawberry would recognize the chunks: a single food. Strain out the fruit and set the juice, and you have jelly, a condiment.
Including the peanut, which is a legume pretending to be a nut.

nodes.trait: Ground or smashed, the whole food and nothing else
nodes.short: The order says what was done to it. Whatever it was, the original still knows it.

nodes.trait: The real family of the peanut
nodes.short: Peas, beans and peanuts.
The real genus of the peanut.
Peanuts that have been smashed a great deal. Still one food, and the peanut knows it: smashing the whole food passes the lineup; extracting a part (like peanut oil) would not.
Smashed until smooth. A variety, like a cut of steak.
Smashed, with some peanut left in pieces. Still the same food, still a variety.

nodes.trait: The swollen underground part of the plant
nodes.short: Potatoes, mostly. Botanically a stem, emotionally a side.
The order says what was done to it. The oil is how it was cooked, not an ingredient.

nodes.trait: The real family of the potato
nodes.short: Potatoes, tomatoes, peppers and eggplants.
The real genus of the potato.

Potatoes, cut and fried. A potato would pick its fries out of a police lineup, so they are a single food; the salt is visiting. Mashed potatoes are another matter: the butter and milk make them combined. Found in the wild beside steak and burgers, in associations.

nodes.trait: From an animal, or made by one
nodes.short: Meat, fish, and what bees make.
Steak and friends.
The order says what was done to it. Whatever it was, the original still knows it.
Cows, and therefore steak.
The real genus of cattle.
One food, grilled. The salt and pepper on top are single foods visiting, and the cow would still recognize it. Cuts such as ribeye and sirloin are varieties, not species.
Raw or otherwise.
The order says what was done to it. Whatever it was, the original still knows it.
Tunas and mackerels.
The real genus of tuna.

Raw tuna, sliced. One food, still recognizable: the tuna would pick it out of a lineup. The soy sauce is a condiment; real wasabi is a grated root and a single food, while the usual green paste was made. Not sushi, because there is no rice.
Honey: nectar, bossed around by bees.
The order says what was done to it. Whatever it was, the original still knows it.

nodes.trait: The real family of the honey bee
nodes.short: Bees, which did all the work.
The real genus of the honey bee.
Nectar, bossed around by bees, still recognizable. Nature made it, so it is a single food, wherever it gets drizzled.
Salt, chiefly. Nature made it.
Salt is salt.
The order says what was done to it. Whatever it was, the original still knows it.

nodes.trait: Rock salt and sea salt, the mineral halite
nodes.short: The salt family, mineralogically.
Table salt, sea salt, kosher salt.
Salt is salt: nature made it, and it is recognizably itself, so it is a single food, not a condiment. Salting a steak does not make the steak a constructed food; the salt is merely visiting.

nodes.trait: The originals can't recognize themselves, or several foods share the job
nodes.short: Where nearly every argument happens. Sorted into phyla by what holds the food together.

nodes.trait: Ingredients fused into one new mass
nodes.short: The building materials: breads, pastas, sausages and cheeses.
Bread in every form: loaves, buns, rolls, tortillas, fried shells, batter. The only material that makes a sandwich.
Bread, toasted. Still constructed, because bread was built from flour, water and yeast.

nodes.trait: Dough cooked in water or steam
nodes.short: Pasta, noodles, dumpling wrappers and steamed buns. Cooked wet, so not bread.

nodes.trait: Meat fused into a new shape
nodes.short: Sausages, franks and meatballs. The frank alone lives here; in a bun it graduates to Involucra.
Cheese.

nodes.trait: Seasoned rice pressed into one mass
nodes.short: Sushi rice: vinegared, seasoned and packed until the grains act as one mass. Not bread, because the grain was never ground into dough. Loose steamed rice does not qualify.

nodes.trait: Fat-rich dough baked into a crust
nodes.short: Shortcrust and puff pastry. Baked like bread, but built from fat as much as flour, which makes it its own material.

nodes.trait: The food is its own plate
nodes.short: A container food holds a filling. What the container is made of decides the class: bread, dough, rice, pastry or a whole food.

nodes.trait: A filling held between bread: bread on opposite sides of the filling
nodes.short: The class this entire website exists to defend. A sandwich is a filling between bread, and only bread qualifies; its cousins in other materials have classes of their own. Sandwiches are sorted by their bread all the way down. The filling is a passenger and is only identified at genus.

nodes.trait: Slices taken from a larger loaf
nodes.short: The classic arrangement your opponents think is the only kind. The bread was a loaf before it was a sandwich.

nodes.trait: Two or more slices cut from a loaf
nodes.short: Undisputed by everyone, which makes them boring.
Cold cuts, bacon, lettuce, whatever fits. The genus every other sandwich is measured against.
The type specimen. Nobody has ever filed an appeal.
Fillings spread rather than stacked. The filling's shape decides the genus, and a spread is a shape.
nodes.trait: A filling spread on the slices

nodes.short: A sandwich: two slices from a loaf with spreads between them. Not bread with condiments: the peanut butter is a single food, and the second spread decides the variety.
Two single foods between bread: peanut butter and strawberry jam.
A single food and a condiment between bread. Nothing in the rules forbids a condiment from joining an assembled food.

nodes.trait: One whole roll, bun, tortilla, pizza dough or coating per sandwich, however it is cut, hinged, folded or sealed
nodes.short: Home of the hot dog, the burger, the sub, the taco and the burrito. The bread was made for this sandwich and nothing else.
nodes.long: A hamburger bun is cut all the way through and a hot dog bun is hinged; both are whole buns, so both are here. Cutting a roll in half before building the sandwich is the same as cutting the sandwich in half after: a more complicated way to reach the same result.

nodes.trait: A baked bun or roll, split, hinged or cut through
nodes.short: If the meatball sub is a sandwich, and everyone agrees it is, the hot dog comes with it. Same bread, different passenger.
Strictly, the genus of tube fillings. It keeps the name Canis for historical reasons, as real biologists keep a misnomer once it sticks.
A sandwich. The filling sits between two walls of bun, which is one more than an open-faced sandwich manages.
nodes.long: Merriam-Webster declared the hot dog a sandwich in 2016, and California and New York tax law agree. The National Hot Dog and Sausage Council disagrees, on the grounds that the hot dog has transcended sandwiches. The Review Board notes that transcending a category requires first belonging to it.

nodes.short: The food court legend: a quarter-pound hot dog and a 20-ounce soda for $1.50, a price unchanged since the mid-1980s. The price is part of the specimen. The $1.50 buys a hot dog and a soda, two specimens, so the deal itself is recorded as the type association of this variety: the Costco combo. The flagship of the taxonomy.
nodes.long: Collected in the wild between the checkout lanes and the exit. Habitat: a metal table, never a chair. Diet of the observer: whatever was in the cart. The specimen is still ordered as "a hot dog," which is why it is a variety and not a species of its own. Diagnostic trait: the $1.50 price tag. Should the price ever change, this variety will be declared extinct and any successor described as a new variety. Since April 2026 a bottle of water may stand in for the soda; the Board considers this normal variation. Two Costco CEOs have been asked about the price on the record. Both said no, one more colorfully.

sources.title: Costco CEO promises the $1.50 hot dog isn't going away: 'The price will not change as long as I'm around'
sources.note: Fortune, via Yahoo Finance, March 2026. Current CEO Ron Vachris.

sources.title: Costco hot dogs have cost $1.50 since the 1980s. Here's why prices aren't changing
sources.note: NPR, June 2024. Includes co-founder and former CEO Jim Sinegal's warning to his successor about raising the price.

nodes.short: "Dragged through the garden" with mustard, relish, onion, tomato, pickle spear, sport peppers and celery salt on a poppy seed bun. Ketchup is grounds for deportation.
New York street cart classic. Unknowable flavor profile.
Wrapped in bacon and piled with beans and toppings. Pushes the variety rule to its limit.
Plain, or ketchup only. Included for completeness, not endorsed.

nodes.trait: A flat round filling: a patty
nodes.short: Burgers. Long accepted as sandwiches by people who reject the hot dog, which this genus finds awkward.
A sandwich. A whole bun, cut all the way through, holding a disc. Exactly as much a sandwich as the hot dog, which shares its family.
Spheres, in a roll, held in place mostly by sauce.
A sandwich nobody disputes, built exactly like a hot dog.
Chunks held together by mayonnaise, butter or optimism.
A hot dog bun with a better lawyer.
Cold cuts, folded and stacked in a roll.
Sheets of cold cuts in a whole roll. Still Integriformes when ordered as a 6-inch.
nodes.long: Subway bakes footlong rolls and cuts them in half to make 6-inch subs. The Board ruled that cutting a roll in half before building the sandwich is the same as cutting the sandwich in half after: a more complicated way to reach the same result. The 6-inch keeps its classification. It is noted here only as a terrible way of making it.

nodes.trait: A whole tortilla, folded or rolled
nodes.short: Griddled flatbread, so it is bread. The hot dog's next-door neighbors.

nodes.trait: A heap of filling: meat, beans, salsa
nodes.short: Whatever fits. How the tortilla closes over it decides the species: folded is a taco, rolled and sealed is a burrito.
A sandwich. Starch on the bottom and both sides, filling in the middle: the same shape as a hot dog bun.
nodes.long: A Massachusetts judge ruled in 2006 that one tortilla is not two slices of bread. A hot dog bun is also one piece, so that logic would expel hot dogs too. The Review Board declines to sacrifice the hot dog.

nodes.short: Fried, not baked. Still Formata: the phylum is about how the food is built, not how it is cooked.
Spit-roasted pork, pineapple and a folded tortilla. A sandwich.
Battered fish, cabbage and crema. A sandwich at the beach.
Fully wrapped, so it is more enclosed than a classic sandwich. A Massachusetts court disagreed in 2006; the court was not consulted on hot dogs.
The bread is fried on, in one piece. Still dough, still bread.
Tubes in batter. The genus name Canis was taken by the hot dog.
A hot dog fully swallowed by its own bun. The hot dog's cousin.

nodes.trait: Pizza dough folded, rolled or lidded over a filling before baking
nodes.short: Pizza that the baker closed. Sealed before baking is preparation, so it is bread on both sides of a filling: a sandwich. The rules are the rules.

nodes.trait: A heap of cheese and fillings
nodes.short: Ricotta, mozzarella, meats and vegetables, sealed in.
A sandwich. Pizza dough folded and sealed before baking, the same move as a taco's fold, made by the baker. Whole bread on both sides of the filling.
A sandwich. Unlike deep dish, it has a second, thin crust on top of the filling, with sauce over that: bread on both sides of the filling.

nodes.trait: Sheets of meat and cheese rolled up in the dough
nodes.short: Cold cuts in a spiral.
A sandwich. Pizza dough rolled around meats and cheese and baked. A sealed, whole bread, like the burrito.

nodes.trait: A container of boiled or steamed dough
nodes.short: Sandwich architecture in a wet-cooked wrapper. A steamed bun is a dumpling, even when folded like a taco.
Pleated dough around a filling, steamed and pan-fried. The wrapper was cooked wet first, so it is a dumpling.
Boiled pasta sealed around a filling. A dumpling with an Italian passport.
A folded bao looks like a taco and is not one. The bun is steamed, not baked, so it is a dumpling.
The sandwich's cousin, not its sibling: the same architecture, but the container is rice, and rice is not bread.

nodes.trait: Pressed rice rolled fully around a filling
nodes.short: Cut a maki roll and the cross-section shows a container on every side with the filling in the middle. A burrito would recognize the shape, but not the material.
Not a sandwich. Pressed sushi rice encloses crab, avocado and cucumber on every side: sandwich architecture, but the container is rice, not bread. So it is sushi.
nodes.long: This ruling settled the question that started everything: what is bread? Bread is ground grain made into dough and baked, griddled or fried. Sushi rice keeps its grains whole, so however tightly it is pressed, it is not bread. The California roll is also an inside-out roll, with rice outside and seaweed within, which is why the rice, not the nori, is the container.

nodes.short: Pressed rice around a filling, often wrapped in nori. The rice is the container, so it is sushi in the broad sense.
Pastry above and below a filling. Not a sandwich, however hard the pot pie argues.
A stew sealed in pastry. The container decides, and pastry is not bread, so it is a pie.
A hand-held pie: pastry folded and sealed around a filling.

nodes.trait: A container that is a whole food (Naturalia), not a made material
nodes.short: Nice try.
A container, but not a dough-based one. A salad in disguise.
Shaped like a hot dog: a split container cradling a filling with condiments. Convergent evolution, not ancestry, because a banana is not bread.
Pizza, lasagna, nachos and cake. Where open-faced sandwiches go to think about what they did.
One base, toppings on top. Sorted like sandwiches: a slice from a loaf, or a whole base made for the dish, then the kind of base.

nodes.trait: Toppings on a slice cut from a larger loaf
nodes.short: The open-faced cousins of the classic sandwich. The bread was a loaf before it was a base.

nodes.trait: A slice or half of an existing loaf
nodes.short: Toast, with ambitions.
Open-faced sandwiches, bruschetta, and the French bread pizza that thinks it is a pizza.
Not a sandwich. One slice is a topping arrangement. It stands or falls with the pizza, and nobody calls pizza a sandwich.
Not a pizza. A split loaf with pizza toppings: the base decides, and its base is part of a loaf. It stands with the open-faced sandwich.

nodes.trait: One whole base made for this dish: a pizza crust, a pad of rice
nodes.short: Every pizza lives here. The base was made for these toppings and nothing else.

nodes.trait: Dough stretched or tossed by hand; nothing shapes it but the baker
nodes.short: Stretched, tossed and slid into the oven. A screen or tray underneath shapes nothing, so it does not count.
Round, flat and adorned. The genus most people picture when they hear "pizza."

The original: a soft, thin, blistered crust from a very hot oven, with few toppings. One base, toppings on top. Folding a slice is proper technique, not reclassification: it is folded by the eater, not the baker.
Tomato, mozzarella and basil. Named, by tradition, for a queen, hence reginae.
Tomato, garlic, oregano, olive oil, and no cheese. Named for sailors, hence nautarum. No seafood was involved.
Large, thin, foldable slices from a big hand-tossed pie. The fold is proper technique and changes nothing: it is folded by the eater, not the baker.
The control group. Sauce and mozzarella.
Pepperoni cupping into small grease reservoirs. A variety, ordered as "a pepperoni slice."
The hand-tossed pie of delivery menus and pizza parlors across the continent: medium crust, cut in wedges, topped generously. Type locality of the Hawaiian.
Pineapple belongs on pizza. The Board has examined the objection and finds it to be a preference in a lab coat.
nodes.long: Topped foods admit any topping on any base, and no rule, here or anywhere, says fruit may not ride on a pizza. The tomato is a fruit, and nobody has disputed the marinara. The pairing is also sound on its own terms: pineapple brings sweetness and acid, ham brings salt and fat, the same balance as a glazed ham, which nobody calls a crime. Classified as a variety, not a species, because it is still ordered as a pizza. Type locality: the Satellite Restaurant in Chatham, Ontario, where Sam Panopoulos is credited with inventing it in the 1960s and naming it after the brand of canned pineapple he used. It is therefore Canadian, and named after a can. Disputes may be filed using the button below; the Board will read them with a slice in hand.

sources.title: Hawaiian Pizza
sources.note: The Canadian Encyclopedia. Credits Sam Panopoulos at the Satellite Restaurant in Chatham, Ontario, and the canned-pineapple name.

nodes.short: The Hawaiian's bolder relative. Pepperoni's heat and salt against pineapple's sweetness. The Board considers this the variety's finest form.
Everything at once: sausage, pepperoni, peppers, onions, olives, mushrooms. Still ordered as a pizza, so still a variety.
Cheese rolled into the rim. The rim is a tiny sealed sandwich, but the assembly rule classifies the structure the whole thing forms: an open-faced pie with a fancy edge.
Chicago's other pizza: a thin, crisp, cracker-like crust, cut in squares. The squares do not make it a species (cutting never counts); the crust does.
Thin, charred and oblong, from coal-fired ovens in New Haven, Connecticut. Its best-known variety is the white clam pie. Species inquirenda: known from reports, not yet collected by the Board.

A cracker-thin crust made without yeast, topped with Provel (a processed blend of cheddar, Swiss and provolone) and cut in squares. Species inquirenda: known from reports, not yet collected by the Board.
Rome's round pizza: rolled very thin and baked crisp. Not to be confused with its pan-shaped namesake, Roman al taglio. Species inquirenda: known from reports, not yet collected by the Board.
From the cities on the Iowa–Illinois border: a crust with malt in it, cut into strips with scissors. Species inquirenda: known from reports, not yet collected by the Board.

Baked with sauce, then topped with cold cheese and toppings after it leaves the oven. Late toppings are still toppings: one base, toppings on top. Species inquirenda: known from reports, not yet collected by the Board.
A thin hand-shaped crust as a stage for unconventional toppings, BBQ chicken being the classic. Species inquirenda: known from reports, not yet collected by the Board.

nodes.trait: The pan shapes the crust: it rises up the sides and takes the pan's form
nodes.short: Pizzas that took the shape of their container. Baking in a pan is not enough; the pan has to do the shaping.
Named for the Latin for frying pan. Thick, square, crisp-edged or deep.
Rectangular, thick and airy, baked in a steel pan with cheese pushed to the edges until it fries into a crisp, caramelized frame. Sauce often goes on top.
Pepperoni, diced bacon and more, on a thick, airy crust with a caramelized cheese frame. Still ordered as a Detroit pizza, so a variety: carnivora, the meat-eating one.
nodes.long: Plate II shows the specimen entire, a cross-section of the crust (about 3.8 cm tall, mostly air), the pepperoni, the diced bacon, the cheese and sauce, and the burnt cheese edge that defines the species. The Board notes that the edge is the point.

nodes.short: Considered and ruled: a pizza. The crust rises up the pan's walls, but walls around an open top are a rim, not "between." The Board heard the casserole and pie arguments and moved on.
nodes.long: Built upside down from the usual order: crust, cheese, fillings, then sauce on top. Ordered as a pizza, eaten with a knife and fork, defended with conviction. Its cousin with a top crust, Chicago stuffed pizza, has bread on both sides of the filling and is a sandwich.

nodes.short: Thick, spongy and square, baked in a sheet pan that shapes it.
Thinner than Sicilian, pressed into an oiled sheet pan, with sauce dotted over the cheese. Aviae: of the grandmother.

Baked in long rectangular pans, sold by weight and cut with scissors. Shares a city with Roman tonda, but the pan shapes it, so it lives with the pan pizzas. Species inquirenda: known from reports, not yet collected by the Board.

nodes.trait: Rice pressed by hand into a base for one piece
nodes.short: Rice keeps its grains, so it is not bread, but the logic is the same: a whole base made for its topping.
Fish on rice. Open-faced sushi.
Not a sandwich. A pressed-rice base with fish on top: an open-faced sushi, in the same order as the pizza.
Lasagna and layer cake.
Layered, with no container. Not a sandwich, and the "is pasta bread?" fight never has to happen.
nodes.long: Lasagna has pasta above and below a filling, which looks like a sandwich until you notice there is no container: just flat layers, stacked. Pasta is also boiled dough, not baked, so the question of whether pasta is bread never has to be answered.

nodes.short: Soup, stew, ramen and cereal. The class level decides which of them are soup.

nodes.trait: Cooked together after assembly, or served in a broth simmered from ingredients
nodes.short: Soup. Either the solids and liquid were cooked together, or the liquid is a broth that was simmered from ingredients before they met. Serving it cold later is fine.
Soup by any definition.
Soup. In a bread bowl it gets complicated; appeals are pending.
Soup. Boiling water is poured over the dried noodles and seasoning, and they cook together in the cup after assembly.
nodes.long: The contrast with cereal is the whole point: cereal meets cold milk and nothing is cooked; cup noodles meet boiling water and cook in place. Same bowl-and-liquid shape, opposite verdict.

nodes.short: Soup. The noodles and broth cook separately and only meet in the bowl, but the broth was simmered from bones and aromatics for hours, and a simmered broth makes a soup.
nodes.long: Ramen forced the soup rule to grow up. Under the original rule (cooked together after assembly) it would not have been soup, and neither would pho. The Board added a second way in: a liquid that is itself a broth simmered from ingredients. Cereal still fails both tests, because milk is not a broth.

nodes.short: Soup. Rice noodles and raw beef meet a broth that simmered for hours; the broth clause covers it, and the hot broth finishes cooking the beef anyway.
Grain simmered in liquid, the same mechanism as chowder. Soup-adjacent, and the reason cold cereal is not.

nodes.trait: Never cooked together, and the liquid is not a broth
nodes.short: Solids in a liquid that was never a broth and never cooked with them. Not soup.

nodes.trait: Solids stay separate in the liquid
nodes.short: You can still pick the pieces out with a spoon.
Not soup. The flakes were toasted and the milk was pasteurized, but they were never cooked together. Not our problem.
Chewy tapioca pearls floating in sweet milk tea. You chew it, so it is food, not a drink, and it shares an order with cereal: solids floating in a cold liquid that was never cooked with them.
nodes.long: The tea alone is a drink. The pearls change its role: like the milkshake, it left Liquida by requiring effort. The extra-wide straw is a vessel and does not count.

nodes.trait: Raw solids blended into one liquid
nodes.short: Gazpacho, milkshakes and smoothies: blended cold, never cooked, and not soup.
Not soup. Traditional gazpacho is raw vegetables blended and served cold, never cooked. The rule holds even when it hurts.
Not a drink and not soup. Ice cream blended with milk is a dessert, and a dessert wearing a straw is still a dessert. Blended cold and never cooked, it shares an order with gazpacho.
Breakfast, so it is food, even through a straw. Fruit and yogurt blended cold: a close relative of gazpacho, and not soup.
Salad, fried rice and stir-fry.
Salad.
Romaine tossed with Caesar dressing, croutons and grilled chicken. Tossed raw, so it lives in Iactatae; the chicken was cooked first, separately, which does not count.
nodes.long: A useful test case: it contains a bread (croutons are Panes), a cooked meat and a condiment, yet it is not a sandwich, because nothing contains anything. It is architecture-free, which is the whole point of Mixta.

nodes.short: Stir-fry, fried rice and mixed casseroles: stirred together, then cooked as one.
Noodles, tuna and sauce stirred together and baked. Mixed, not layered, so it lives in Mixta.
nodes.long: Casserole is a pan, not a phylum. Casseroles are sorted by how they are built: layered ones, like lasagna or shepherd's pie, go to Stratifica; mixed ones, like this, go to Mixta.

nodes.short: A real biology term for organisms nobody can place. Ours holds candy corn, Jell-O salad and gas station sushi.
Under review since roughly 1880.
Contains elements of every phylum. The Board has recused itself.

associations.short: Steak and fries, served together and eaten in separate bites. Two species living side by side: an association, not a new species. The menu name never creates a specimen.
associations.long: Named in the ecologists' style, after its dominant members (Bos and Solanum) with the ending -etum, as a beech wood is a Fagetum. Béarnaise, when present, is a condiment applied to the steak, not a member.

associations.short: A quarter-pound hot dog and a 20-ounce soda for $1.50. The type association of the Costco hot dog: the price that defines the variety buys both. If the price changes, the variety goes extinct, and its type association with it.
associations.long: The soda is a fountain cola, poured by the member of the public. The hot dog is still a sandwich.

associations.short: A hamburger, fries and a fountain soda, ordered as one item and eaten as three. An association: every member can be eaten in separate bites, and each keeps its own classification.
associations.long: Named after its two dominant members, Discus and Solanum, as ecologists do. The soda is an associate. Any toy in the bag is a commensal: noted, never classified.
